findings.body: Both scripts install `symphony-forge==1.1.0` (Windows: scripts/install-windows.ps1:61). [uv resolves a bare package name from an index by default](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/indexes/), while README.md:119 and docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:47-48 define this release as the GitHub tag `v1.1.0` and install it from Git. The scripts therefore do not select the release the repository names; on a clean laptop, Forge installation may fail before the final version check. Install the tagged Git source using the script’s version variable.
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — install the named Forge release

findings.body: Using `npm.cmd` lets installation run under Windows PowerShell’s default Restricted policy, but npm also creates `.ps1` shims for installed commands. A salesperson who follows the printed next step and types `claude` or `codex` in PowerShell can hit the same execution-policy block; the script gives no usable command or recovery step. [npm documents its PowerShell shims](https://github.com/npm/rfcs/blob/main/implemented/0032-powershell-bins.md), and [Microsoft documents the Restricted default](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_execution_policies?view=powershell-5.1). Make the installed agents usable through the promised PowerShell flow.
findings.title: Not done: One script sets up a laptop — usable Windows agent commands

findings.body: The Windows tests invoke the script only with `powershell -File`; none exercises the promised `irm … | iex` entry point. That leaves the user-facing invocation untested even though the Mac test exercises piped Bash. Add an isolated full-run test that evaluates the Windows script as the one-liner does, with third-party commands stubbed.
findings.title: Not done: Windows piped install test

findings.body: The head commit’s `Functional check:` paragraph records Mac observations but says the Windows check, install, all-present and WSL2 test result is still pending. The plan here requires observed stubbed runs for both scripts. Record the Windows outcomes, including the WSL2 guidance; the specified clean-laptop checks may remain with the owner after merge.
findings.title: Not done: functional check

findings.body: Any directory matching each browser prefix counts as installed, including obsolete or incomplete downloads; Windows uses the same predicate at scripts/install-windows.ps1:21. Check mode can therefore list nothing missing while the Playwright version used by a project cannot launch a browser. [Playwright requires browser binaries specific to its version](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers). Check usable revisions and executables before skipping installation.
findings.title: Check usable Playwright revisions before skipping installation

findings.body: If `docker` is already on PATH from a CLI-only install, this check skips the Docker cask even when there is no Docker Desktop or working engine. Windows similarly treats any `docker` command as proof that Desktop is installed at scripts/install-windows.ps1:50. In that case the laptop still cannot run the Docker-based prototype tests. Check the usable Docker installation, or give the user the step needed to start it.
findings.title: Treat a Docker CLI without Docker Desktop as missing

findings.body: Done-when item 2 calls for running each script with a one-liner from the checklist, but the checklist and README link are assigned to SPEC on this line and are not present in this branch. SPEC needs to publish the `curl … | bash` and `irm … | iex` commands before that user path is complete.
